title: Keep nested Opus option lookups in separate hash tables
problem: The unnumbered application-value lookup replaces the active outer hash slot while const_str_hash scans lib/opus.c. Consequently vbr and packet_loss, which appear after that nested switch, are generated into the application table and can never be recognized as encoder option keys.
reproduce: At 25ac052c, generating lib/opus.c with WITH_TRANSCODING produces an outer table with only complexity, compression_level, and application; packet_loss and vbr are absent and the outer lookup returns no match for them.
acceptance: The generated outer table contains all seven Opus encoder option spellings, the nested table contains the seven application spellings, and the focused constant-string hash executable recognizes entries before, inside, and after a nested lookup.
repair: Assign the nested application-value switch to numbered lookup slot 1, leaving the surrounding encoder-option switch in slot 0, and add a focused nested-table regression to the existing const_str_hash test.

verification.limitations: BCL verifies generated lookup membership and executes the focused C hash test in Linux. It does not run a live rtpengine call or inspect encoded Opus packets.
verification.ownerCheck: Set packet_loss=10 on the affected Opus transcode path and confirm the unknown-option warning disappears and in-band FEC packets are produced when the peer offers useinbandfec=1.

publish.commitMessage: Fix nested Opus option hash lookups
